new_lead.title: A Blind Trust, the Bloody Thrust: lifecycle-hook supply-chain risk for AI agent harnesses
verified_facts: arXiv lists the paper in the Friday, September 4, 2026 cs.CR batch.
The paper studies attacker-controlled lifecycle-hook/plugin updates in AI agent harnesses where hook commands can execute with host privileges.
The authors describe HookPry as an open-source automated framework and report 1,000 end-to-end runs across 25 harness/backend combinations and seven evaluated harnesses.
The reported compromise and defense metrics are author claims from a new preprint and have not been independently reproduced in this pass.
new_lead.safety_boundary: Evaluate only defensive architecture, artifact integrity, permission-manifest and update-verification implications. Do not execute the offensive framework against real or third-party systems.
missing_verification: Locate and verify the paper's official code repository and license rather than relying on the abstract's open-source claim alone.
Review the exact harnesses/backends, lifecycle-hook update assumptions, privilege model, attack objectives and defensive baselines in the full paper.
Reproduce only benign/local fixture checks relevant to plugin/skill update integrity and hook permission boundaries.
new_lead.recommended_action: Integrity/Build should compare this threat model against the repository's installed-plugin/skill and recurring-agent supply-chain surfaces, then consider deterministic integrity/permission tests without importing offensive capability.
